APT-ENG-12471:
**Tense & Passive to Active Rule:**
- The given sentence is in the **Simple Present Tense** in the passive voice:
  $$\text{Object} + \text{is/am/are} + \text{not} + \text{V3} + \text{by} + \text{Subject}$$
- The corresponding active voice structure is:
  $$\text{Subject} + \text{do/does not} + \text{V1 (base verb)} + \text{Object} + \text{Adverb}$$
- The active subject **"Hikers"** is plural, requiring the auxiliary **"do not"** followed by the base verb **"visit"**: *"Hikers do not visit this trail frequently."*

**Distractor Analysis:**
- **Option A:** Uses ungrammatical auxiliary syntax (*"not have frequently visit"*).
- **Option B:** Uses singular auxiliary *"does not"* with the plural subject *"Hikers"* (subject-verb agreement error).
- **Option D:** Uses past auxiliary *"did not"*, altering the tense from Simple Present to Simple Past.

Hence, **Option C** is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-12472:
**Tense & Active to Passive Rule:**
- The active sentence is in the **Simple Present Tense** (`Subject + V1 + Object`).
- The passive voice rule for Simple Present is:
  $$\text{Object} + \text{is/am/are} + \text{V3 (past participle)} + \text{by} + \text{Subject}$$
- The object **"The roads"** is plural, requiring the plural auxiliary **"are"** followed by the past participle **"fixed"**: *"The roads are fixed by indentured labourers."*

**Distractor Analysis:**
- **Option A:** Uses singular past auxiliary *"was"*, violating both tense and subject-verb agreement.
- **Option B:** Uses past auxiliary *"were"*, altering the tense to Simple Past.
- **Option D:** Uses *"were being fixed"*, changing the tense to Past Continuous.

Hence, **Option C** is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-12473:
**Grammatical Rule (Placement of Adverbs of Frequency):**
- Adverbs of frequency (e.g., *always, never, usually, hardly ever*) must be placed **before the main verb** (or immediately after an auxiliary verb/verb *to be*).
- In Option C, *"always"* is incorrectly placed after the main lexical verb *"arrives"*.
- **Correct phrasing:** *"Nila **always arrives** on time for meetings."*
- Options A, B, and D correctly position their adverbs (*never*, *hardly ever*, *usually*) before the main verb *arrives*.

Hence, **Option C** is the correct answer.

APT-ENG-12477:
**Grammatical Rule:**
- **"Seldom"** is an adverb of frequency meaning "rarely" or "not often." It cannot be combined with the comparative conjunction **"than"** to indicate a preference.
- To express preference over an alternative before a gerund, the comparative phrase **"Rather than"** (or prepositional phrase *"Instead of"*) must be used.

**Error Analysis:**
- Segment B, *"Seldom than walking,"* contains an erroneous adverbial construction.
- **Correct phrasing:** *"**Rather than** walking, she prefers to take the city bus."*

Hence, **Option B** is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-12478:

**Classification of other options:**
- **Twice:** Adverb of frequency/number (answers *how many times*).
- **Often:** Adverb of frequency (answers *how often*).
- **Happily:** Adverb of manner (answers *how/in what manner*).

Hence, **Option C** is the correct answer.

APT-ENG-12480:
**Tense & Active to Passive Rule:**
- The active sentence is in the **Simple Future Tense** (`Subject + will + V1 + Object`).
- The passive voice rule for Simple Future is:
  $$\text{Object} + \text{will} + \text{be} + \text{V3 (past participle)} + \text{by} + \text{Subject}$$
- The past participle of the irregular verb *build* is **built**.
- Applying the rule: *"An amphitheatre will be built by the government."*

**Distractor Analysis:**
- **Option A:** Uses the base form *"build"* instead of the past participle *"built"*.
- **Option C:** Changes the modal auxiliary *"will"* to *"would"*.
- **Option D:** Omits the auxiliary *"will"* and retains the base form *"build"*.

Hence, **Option B** is the correct answer.

APT-ENG-12482:
**Tense & Modal Perfect Rule:**
- The active sentence uses a **Modal Perfect** construction (`Subject + might + have + V3 + Object`).
- The passive voice rule for modal perfect is:
  $$\text{Object} + \text{modal} + \text{have} + \text{been} + \text{V3} + \text{by} + \text{Subject}$$
- Applying the rule:
  - Object: *"Mira"*
  - Auxiliary: *"might have been"*
  - Past participle: *"delayed"*
  - Agent: *"by the snow-storm"*
  - Result: *"Mira might have been delayed by the snow-storm."*

**Distractor Analysis:**
- **Option B:** Unnecessarily shifts the modal to *"may"* and drops the perfect aspect (*"may be delayed"*).
- **Option C:** Drops the perfect aspect (*"might be delayed"*).
- **Option D:** Changes the modal from *"might"* to *"may"*.

Hence, **Option A** is the correct answer.
APT-ENG-12483:
**Tense & Active to Passive Rule:**
- The active sentence is in the **Simple Past Tense** (`Subject + V2 + Object`).
- The passive voice rule for Simple Past is:
  $$\text{Object} + \text{was/were} + \text{V3 (past participle)} + \text{by} + \text{Subject}$$
- The object **"All the pastries"** is plural, requiring the plural auxiliary **"were"** followed by the past participle **"eaten"**: *"All the pastries were eaten by the cat."*

**Distractor Analysis:**

- **Option C:** Uses past perfect auxiliary *"had been"*, altering the tense.

Hence, **Option B** is the correct answer.
